findings.evidence: description names jev backends but has no clause for requests that do not name jev
findings.fix: Use when a fast, cheap typed judgment beats a full reasoning pass: a yes/no (noul), picking among named options (choice), a rubric score (score), or screening evidence against a criterion, even when the user only asks for a quick second opinion or a triage call without naming jev. Runs through the shared System One client on Laya (local), TypeSafe or OpenCode Zen (remote, consent required). Advisory only: needs_fallback means you decide that item yourself, and no answer is a verdict or gate. Not for building TypeSafe into an app (typesafe-ai) or for editing code.

Gate the four external links by a condition, for example 'Fetch the Confidence page only when you are interpreting probabilities beyond reference.md ## Interpreting answers'. Otherwise drop them, because reference.md already summarizes 1.14 and confidence.
Say when GSD_PATH_JEV=1 is required and when it must be left out, or remove it from the generic caller example so callers do not copy a flag they do not understand.

findings.evidence: Most should-trigger queries name jev, Laya or TypeSafe explicitly (for example 'Quick yes or no from jev', 'Ask TypeSafe to pick').
findings.fix: Replace 3-4 should-trigger queries with prompts that state the need without naming jev, such as 'cheap quick triage: is this CI failure noise or real? don't burn a full analysis'. These test whether the description triggers on its own.
